Cut samples into epochs around sync port pulses

Source: R/sync.R
g3_epochs.Rd

Returns the samples from before seconds before to after seconds after the onset of each sync port pulse, for example to analyse pupil responses to stimuli whose onset was marked with a sync pulse. With several recordings, each recording is cut at its own pulses.

Usage

g3_epochs(
  x,
  events,
  before = 0,
  after = 1,
  direction = c("out", "in"),
  pulses = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A data frame with a time column, such as the output of read_g3_gaze() or read_g3_imu().

events

Event data from read_g3_events().

before, after

Seconds to keep before and after each onset.

direction

"out" for the signal sent by the glasses, "in" for the signal received from external equipment.

pulses

Which pulses to use, as pulse numbers. Defaults to all.

Value

The selected rows of x, sorted by time within each epoch, with added columns pulse and epoch_time (seconds relative to the pulse onset). Samples can appear in more than one epoch if epochs overlap. If x is a grouped tibble, the result has the same groups.

Examples

rec <- read_g3(g3_example())
ep <- g3_epochs(rec$gaze, rec$events, before = 1, after = 5)
dplyr::count(ep, pulse)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 2
#>   pulse     n
#>   <int> <int>
#> 1     1   253
#> 2     2   300
#> 3     3   300
#> 4     4   299
#> 5     5   300
